revoke.title: Revoke certificate
revoke.reasonHelp: RFC 5280 CRL reason. Recorded in the audit log.
revoke.cascade: Also revoke the {count} certificate(s) signed by this one
revoke.warningCa: Revocation is recorded in this application only. It does not remove the certificate from any trust store, and there is no CRL or OCSP endpoint to publish it yet — clients will keep trusting this CA until the certificate expires or is removed from the trust store manually.
revoke.warningLeaf: Revocation is recorded in this application only. This app publishes no CRL or OCSP endpoint yet, so already-distributed certificates keep working until they expire — pair it with removing the certificate from the relying systems.

delete.title: Delete certificate
delete.warningCascade: This deletes the private key material and {count} certificate(s) signed by it, immediately and irreversibly. If you only need to invalidate it, revoke instead.
delete.warning: This deletes the private key material immediately and irreversibly. This cannot be undone.

vault.title: Unlock private keys
vault.firstTimeIntro: Certificate private keys are stored encrypted. Choose a {password} to protect them — this becomes the password you enter whenever LocalCA needs to sign or export a key.
vault.intro: Private keys are encrypted at rest. Enter your vault password to use them for signing and export.
vault.noRecoveryWarning: {lead} If you forget this password, every private key under this account becomes permanently unreadable — including any CA key. Nobody, including an administrator, can reset it.
vault.passwordHelp: At least 8 characters. Longer is better; this guards your CA keys offline.

p12.title: Download PKCS12
p12.intro: Export {name} and its private key as a single {extension} bundle.
p12.warning: {lead} note the password down. It cannot be recovered; if you forget it you will have to export the bundle again.
p12.passwordNote: The export password is required: the bundle contains a private key and is never written to disk unencrypted.
